title: Preemption-order race causes VIP tenant cold-starts and burst shortfalls
creator: Aisha Natarajan
description:
Summary:
High-severity escalation from two enterprise customers (VaultMed & CartoPay) after sustained burst traffic. They observed large clusters of VIP tenant requests being routed to cold workers resulting in 3-8s token-latency spikes and rapid depletion of burst credits. Impacted features: real-time chat and multi-turn inference on dedicated pools.

Observed behavior:
- During combined normal load + rolling maintenance windows, the scale reconciler and preemption logic raced when selecting preemptible nodes to release.
- The preemption selection currently prefers the newest nodes first; when mixed with the allocator's LRU slot steal, this caused hot tenant sessions to be torn down preferentially.
- Reconciler marked freed slots as available before the tenant-level burst-credit accounting job ran, allowing new requests to land on workers that had lost the warmed KV cache and had stale burst budgets.
- Net effect: many VIP sessions hit cold KV cache + exhausted burst credits => backlog to fallback models and customer-facing errors.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
1) Preemption order is biased (LIFO) and not affinity-aware for pinned/VIP sessions.
2) Reconciler ordering allows a window where capacity appears available but tenant accounting is inconsistent (race between capacity mark-ready and burst-credit top-up).
3) No per-tenant hot-worker protection during scale-in; allocator greedily reassigns slots leading to churn.

Work completed so far:
- Reproduced in staging with synthetic VIP workload and rolling drains (staging-grafana: dashboard /d/ai/reserved-pool-burst).
- Added high-resolution tracing to allocator and reconciler (trace IDs: r-2025-02-13-alloc).
- Emergency patch (PR #13429) deployed to staging that defers marking slots READY until tenant burst accounting completes. Initial staging run shows 40% reduction in cold-start rate.

Planned fixes and trade-offs:
- Short-term hotfix (target: roll to prod in next 48h): defer READY marking and add lightweight tenant affinity check to preemption selector to avoid killing nodes with >30% of VIP slots. Trade-off: slightly higher cost due to slower scale-in.
- Medium-term (Q2): implement affinity-aware preemptible ordering and a per-pool grace window during reconciler churn. This requires changes to allocator indices and new metrics. Trade-off: moderate engineering effort (4-6w) but reduces customer impact and burst churn.
- Long-term: introduce a per-tenant pinned-cache signal and a durability contract for KV warm state (possible kernel-level caching hints). Higher complexity and infra changes.

Action items:
- [P0] Roll hotfix to prod with 30m canary, monitor VIP 99th latency and burst-credit balance (owner: Miguel).
- [P1] Add unit + integration tests for preemption ordering (owner: Priya Shah).
- [P1] Instrument a new metric: pool.preemption.vip_protected_count and a dashboard for it (owner: SRE oncall).
- [P2] Draft design doc for affinity-aware preemption (link below).
